title: What the Trace Shows and What the Label Says: Auditing Behavioral Detectors in Agent Evaluation
title_zh: 轨迹显示了什么与标签说了什么：审计智能体评估中的行为检测器

paragraphs.en: LLM agents are often evaluated by reducing execution traces to labels such as final-answer correctness, tool verification, and fault propagation. These labels are useful, but they are measurements produced by parsers, behavioral detectors, and harness rules. We study what happens when those measurements do not fully capture the trace’s behavior. We use GSM8K, a benchmark of grade-school arithmetic word problems, in a tool-use setting where agents can call a calculator whose outputs are occasionally corrupted. This gives us a clear ground truth for the expected tool result and allows us to compare what the calculator returned, what the model later used, and what the automated detectors reported. We audit three trace-level detectors across six production models and 30 problems per model. We find that final correctness, visible re-verification, and fault propagation can disagree in systematic ways. An important failure mode is the silent tool-output override. In these cases, the calculator first returns a corrupted value, but the model later uses a different, often correct, value without calling the calculator again. The bad value may therefore stop propagating even though a verification detector that looks for explicit re-execution records no visible re-check. Human review of 90 traces shows perfect agreement with the reviewed comparable cases for final correctness (67/67), fault recovery/impact (19/19), and fault relevance (18/18), but only 67/81 agreement for verification. All 14 verification disagreements fall into four recurring patterns: repeated calculator calls from stuck loops, verbal recognition of an incorrect tool result without recomputation, repeated expressions within a single reasoning step, and quiet correction after an incorrect value is observed. We also find that execution limits affect the reported result. In an ablation study across two models, one model ranges from 21/30 to 27/30 correct as step and token budgets change, while another remains between 27/30 and 29/30. These findings motivate measurement transparency: an automated label should be accompanied by trace evidence supporting it, whether the detector’s question applied to that trace, whether the run ended early due to an execution limit, and any human corrections to the label. Our trace viewer makes this information inspectable alongside the reported results.
paragraphs.zh: LLM 智能体的评估通常是将执行轨迹归约为一些标签来进行，例如最终答案正确性、工具验证和故障传播。 这些标签很有用，但它们是由解析器、行为检测器和测试框架规则产生的测量结果。 我们研究当这些测量未能完整刻画轨迹行为时会发生什么。 我们使用 GSM8K（一个小学算术应用题基准）在一个工具使用场景中进行研究，其中智能体可以调用一个计算器，而该计算器的输出偶尔会被破坏。 这为我们提供了关于预期工具结果的明确基准真值，并使我们能够比较计算器实际返回的值、模型之后使用的值，以及自动检测器所报告的结果。 我们在六个生产级模型上、每个模型 30 道题的设置下，审计了三个轨迹级检测器。 我们发现，最终正确性、可见的重新验证以及故障传播之间可能以系统性的方式出现分歧。 一个重要的失败模式是静默的工具输出覆盖。 在这些情况下，计算器首先返回一个被破坏的值，但模型之后在没有再次调用计算器的情况下使用了一个不同的、通常是正确的值。 因此，即使查找显式重新执行的验证检测器没有记录到任何可见的重新检查，错误值也可能停止传播。 对 90 条轨迹的人工审查显示，在最终正确性（67/67）、故障恢复/影响（19/19）和故障相关性（18/18）上与被审查的可比案例完全一致，但在验证上只有 67/81 的一致性。 全部 14 个验证分歧可归入四种反复出现的模式：由卡死循环导致的重复计算器调用、在不重新计算的情况下口头确认一个错误的工具结果、单个推理步骤内的重复表达式，以及在观察到错误值之后的悄然纠正。 我们还发现执行限制会影响所报告的结果。 在跨两个模型的消融研究中，一个模型的正确率随步骤和 token 预算的变化在 21/30 到 27/30 之间波动，而另一个模型则保持在 27/30 到 29/30 之间。 这些发现提出了测量透明度的要求：自动标签应附带支持它的轨迹证据，包括检测器所针对的问题是否适用于该轨迹、该次运行是否因执行限制而提前结束，以及任何对标签的人工修正。 我们的轨迹查看器使这些信息可以与所报告的结果一起被查看。

paragraphs.en: Agent evaluation is a measurement process. An agent produces an execution trace—a record of its model and tool interactions—which a parser or detector maps to a label. Labels are then aggregated into numbers such as accuracy, verification rate, or fault-propagation rate. Those numbers are often treated as facts about the agent. In practice, they also depend on the instruments used to measure the agent.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体评估是一个测量过程。 智能体会产生一条执行轨迹——即其模型与工具交互的记录——解析器或检测器会将其映射为一个标签。 这些标签随后被聚合为数字，例如准确率、验证率或故障传播率。 这些数字常常被当作关于智能体的事实。 在实践中，它们还取决于用于测量智能体的工具。

sents.zh: 在实践中，它们还取决于用于测量智能体的工具。

paragraphs.en: This distinction matters because agents are increasingly evaluated for tool use and multi-step decision-making. In such settings, a small measurement mistake can change the interpretation of a run. A trace may contain a correct answer that the parser does not extract. A detector may ask a question that is not meaningful for a particular event. A step limit may stop an agent before it finishes, but the benchmark may still count the run as simply wrong. In higher-stakes settings, such as clinical, defense, or other safety-critical workflows, this kind of false confidence is especially dangerous: an agent can look most trustworthy exactly when it is quietly overriding its instruments. Knowing that an agent received a score is not enough; we also need to know whether the score reflects a trustworthy measurement.
paragraphs.zh: 这一区别之所以重要，是因为对智能体的评估日益聚焦于工具使用和多步决策。 在这类场景中，一个微小的测量错误就可能改变对一次运行的解读。 一条轨迹中可能包含正确答案，但解析器未能将其提取出来。 检测器可能提出的问题对某个特定事件来说并无意义。 步数上限可能在智能体完成任务之前就将其停止，但基准测试可能仍把该次运行简单地计为错误。 在风险更高的场景中，例如临床、国防或其他安全关键型工作流，这种虚假的信心尤其危险：智能体可能恰恰在它悄然覆盖自身工具结果之时，看起来最为可信。 知道智能体获得了一个分数是不够的；我们还需要知道该分数是否反映了可信的测量。

paragraphs.en: Recent work has already shown that the reliability of the evaluator cannot be assumed. Agent benchmark audits find disagreement between automated evaluators and human annotators, tool-calling benchmarks contain brittle judging rules, and agent performance can depend on the harness in which the model is run ( Bean et al., 2025 ; Gurram, 2026 ; Bhat et al., 2026 ; Yao et al., 2026 ) . We build on that line of work, but focus on a narrower question: when an automated trace detector reports a label, did the trace actually contain the right evidence for that label to be interpreted safely?

paragraphs.en: We study the question in a deliberately simple domain. Agents solve arithmetic word problems using a calculator tool. The calculator sometimes returns a plausible but wrong value. Because arithmetic has external ground truth, we can check four things separately: what the calculator should have returned, what it actually returned, what value the model later used, and what final answer the model gave. This makes the setting useful for auditing the measurement apparatus itself.

paragraphs.en: The motivating failure is silent tool-output override. A model receives a corrupted calculator result, but later uses a different value, often the independently correct one, without calling the calculator again and without explicitly stating that the tool was wrong. Prior work on tool-memory conflict already shows that models arbitrate between internal knowledge and tool outputs ( Cheng et al., 2025 ; Varlamov et al., 2026 ) . Our claim is not that this behavior is newly discovered, but that it creates a measurement problem. For example, if the calculator returns 29 for a quantity whose correct value is 30 and the model later continues its reasoning with 30 without another tool call, a propagation detector may correctly record that 29 was not reused while a verification detector still reports no visible re-check. The trace therefore contains evidence of recovery that the verification detector was not designed to represent.

paragraphs.en: Measurement transparency for trace detectors. We define a practical reporting principle for agent evaluation: a detector label should be accompanied by the evidence that supports it, whether the detector was applicable, whether execution was censored, and any known measurement risks or human corrections.

paragraphs.en: A controlled audit of detector reliability. Across six production models, we show that final correctness, visible verification, and fault propagation can diverge in systematic ways, including silent override, inconclusive propagation, formatting failures, and harness-dependent censoring. We also compare automated labels with human review.

paragraphs.en: Evaluator validity. Construct-validity work argues that a benchmark score is meaningful only when the task and metric support the claim being made from them ( Bean et al., 2025 ) . Recent audits make this concern concrete for agents. AgentProp-Bench compares automated judging protocols with human labels and studies error propagation in tool-using agents ( Gurram, 2026 ) . Bhat et al. (2026) audit several tool-calling benchmark families and report evaluator-human disagreements, brittle deterministic rules, judge variance, and corrected benchmark components. REFLECT similarly meta-evaluates LLM judges using controlled interventions on agent traces and finds substantial failure in fine-grained failure detection ( Wang et al., 2026 ) . AgentJudgeBench studies judge reliability specifically for structured tool-calling workflows ( Verma et al., 2026 ) . Our work is complementary: rather than evaluating an LLM judge as a whole, we focus on behavioral trace detectors and ask whether a detector had the observable and applicable evidence needed to support its label.
paragraphs.zh: 评估者的有效性。 构念效度方面的研究指出，只有当任务和指标能够支持从中得出的结论时，基准测试的分数才有意义（Bean et al., 2025）。 近期的审计使这一担忧对智能体而言变得具体化。 AgentProp-Bench 将自动评判协议与人工标注进行比较，并研究工具使用型智能体中的错误传播（Gurram, 2026）。Bhat et al. （2026）审计了多个工具调用基准测试族，并报告了评估者与人类之间的分歧、脆弱的确定性规则、评判者的方差以及修正后的基准测试组件。 REFLECT 同样通过对智能体轨迹进行受控干预来对 LLM 评判者进行元评估，发现其在细粒度失败检测方面存在大量失误（Wang et al., 2026）。 AgentJudgeBench 专门研究结构化工具调用工作流中评判者的可靠性（Verma et al., 2026）。 我们的工作是互补性的：我们不将 LLM 评判者作为一个整体来评估，而是聚焦于行为轨迹检测器，并探究检测器是否拥有支持其标签所需的可观察且适用的证据。

paragraphs.en: Trace- and process-level evaluation. Recent work increasingly evaluates how an agent reaches an outcome rather than only whether it succeeds. ClawTrack separates task success from process quality and includes result verification as a process dimension ( Wu et al., 2026 ) . CTF-ABACUS reconstructs agent trajectories to distinguish demonstrated exploitation from shortcut or unsupported success in cybersecurity tasks ( Milner et al., 2026 ) . paragraphs.en: Agent behavior under faulty tool outputs. A growing set of studies injects wrong or misleading tool outputs and measures how agents respond. Zhang et al. (2026) corrupt search and calculator feedback and find that persistent misleading feedback can leave an agent worse off than receiving no feedback at all. Mittal (2026) perturbs a single tool output in otherwise successful trajectories and finds that most runs recover, often without acknowledging the earlier error, and that fluent wrong evidence is rarely noticed. ToxicBench ( Tao and Yin, 2026 ) rewrites successful tool observations for data agents and reports how often agents comply blindly, flag a problem, run a check, or adopt the corrupted value even after checking. Kaynar et al. (2026) inject faults into a sandboxed multi-tool environment and find that agents often build confident answers on faulted data. These studies characterize what agents do when a tool is wrong. Our focus is complementary: we ask whether the automated labels used to report those behaviors, such as “verified” or “recovered,” match what the trace actually shows.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体在工具输出出错时的行为。 越来越多的研究注入错误或具有误导性的工具输出，并衡量智能体如何应对。Zhang 等人 （2026）破坏搜索与计算器的反馈，发现持续存在的误导性反馈可能使智能体的处境比完全得不到反馈还要糟糕。 Mittal（2026）在原本成功的轨迹中扰动单个工具输出，发现大多数运行都能恢复，且往往不会承认先前出现的错误，而流利但错误的证据几乎不会被察觉。 ToxicBench（Tao 和 Yin，2026）针对数据类智能体重写成功的工具观测结果，并报告智能体盲目遵从、标记问题、运行检查、或在检查之后仍采用被污染数值的频率。Kaynar 等人 （2026）在一个沙盒化的多工具环境中注入故障，发现智能体常常基于故障数据构建出自信的答案。 这些研究刻画了当工具出错时智能体的行为。 我们的关注点是互补的：我们追问用于报告这些行为的自动化标签，例如「已验证」或「已恢复」，是否与轨迹实际显示的内容相符。

paragraphs.en: Harness effects. Harness-Bench shows that agent performance should often be reported at the model-harness configuration level rather than as a property of the model alone ( Yao et al., 2026 ) . Here, the evaluation harness—the runtime configuration governing execution limits and tool behavior—matters because step and token limits can censor traces, while per-call fault injection gives different fault exposure to agents that make different numbers of tool calls. These are not just engineering details; they change what the reported denominator means.
paragraphs.zh: 测试脚手架效应。 Harness-Bench 表明，智能体性能通常应以模型-脚手架配置的层面来报告，而不是仅作为模型本身的属性（Yao et al., 2026）。 在这里，评估脚手架——即控制执行限制和工具行为的运行时配置——之所以重要，是因为步数和 token 限制可能会截断轨迹，而每次调用的故障注入会给调用不同数量工具的智能体带来不同的故障暴露。 这些不只是工程细节；它们会改变所报告分母的含义。

paragraphs.en: Agents solve GSM8K ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ) arithmetic word problems in a ReAct-style loop with access to a calculator. In this loop, the model alternates between reasoning about the problem, choosing whether to call the calculator, observing the returned result, and continuing until it produces a final answer. The prompt instructs the model to use the calculator for arithmetic and to finish with a final numerical answer. During evaluation, the calculator usually returns the correct result. With a configured per-call probability, the fault injector instead returns a plausible wrong number, such as a small offset or digit transposition. Faults are seeded per question, so the random fault schedule is reproducible across runs where comparable tool calls occur. The model is not told that the calculator has been corrupted.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体在 ReAct 风格的循环中解决 GSM8K（Cobbe et al., 2021）算术应用题，并可以使用计算器。 在这个循环中，模型在推理问题、决定是否调用计算器、观察返回结果之间交替进行，直到产生最终答案。 提示词指示模型使用计算器进行算术运算，并以一个最终数值答案收尾。 在评估过程中，计算器通常返回正确结果。 故障注入器会按配置的每次调用概率，转而返回一个看似合理的错误数字，例如一个小的偏移量或数字换位。 故障按问题逐一设定种子，因此在出现可比工具调用的运行之间，随机故障调度是可复现的。 模型不会被告知计算器已被篡改。

paragraphs.en: This section presents the controlled detector audit in C2 . We first compare detector outputs across six production models as shown in Table 4 , then examine trace patterns that make those outputs difficult to interpret, test the effect of harness constraints, and finally compare the automated labels with human review.

paragraphs.en: The clearest measurement gap is silent tool-output override. A calculator returns a corrupted value, but the trace later uses a different value, often the independently correct one, without a calculator re-check. D-impact may therefore record non-propagation while D-verify records no visible verification. Figure 1(b) shows a representative example: the calculator returns a corrupted value, but the model later continues with the correct value without rerunning the tool. The recovery is visible in the trace even though D-verify records no explicit re-check. The detector can therefore be working as defined while still asking a narrower question than the behavior of interest: visible re-execution is not the same as recovery.
paragraphs.zh: 最明显的测量缺口是工具输出的静默覆盖。 计算器返回了一个损坏的值，但轨迹后续使用了另一个不同的值（通常恰好是独立正确的值），而没有重新检查计算器。 因此，D-impact 可能记录为未传播，而 D-verify 记录为没有可见的验证。 图 1(b) 展示了一个典型例子：计算器返回了一个损坏的值，但模型后来在没有重新运行该工具的情况下继续使用了正确的值。 尽管 D-verify 记录中没有显式的重新检查，但这一恢复过程在轨迹中是可见的。 因此，检测器可能完全按定义正常工作，但仍在问一个比目标行为更窄的问题：可见的重新执行并不等同于恢复。

paragraphs.en: We hand-reviewed 90 of 180 traces across the six production models on four dimensions: fault recovery, verification behavior, fault relevance, and final-answer correctness. Human labels were compared with automated labels where the measurement was applicable, and corrections were stored without replacing the original detector output. Agreement therefore describes the reviewed comparable cases rather than all 180 traces.
paragraphs.zh: 我们对六个生产模型的180条轨迹中的90条进行了人工审查，涵盖四个维度：故障恢复、验证行为、故障相关性以及最终答案的正确性。 在测量适用的情况下，将人工标注与自动标注进行比较，修正结果被保存下来，但不替换原始检测器的输出。 因此，一致性描述的是经过审查的可比较案例，而非全部180条轨迹。

paragraphs.en: Manual review also revealed coverage gaps in the automated detection logic, including traces with no obvious anomaly and cases where the initial rules did not capture relevant behavior. We revised the detector logic to cover these cases, reran the automated labels, and re-checked previously reviewed traces against the revised outputs. The agreement results below therefore compare the final detector implementation with the final set of human-reviewed labels.
paragraphs.zh: 人工复核还揭示了自动检测逻辑中存在的覆盖缺口，包括没有明显异常的追踪记录，以及初始规则未能捕捉到相关行为的情况。 我们修订了检测器逻辑以覆盖这些情况，重新运行了自动标注，并根据修订后的输出重新检查了此前已复核的追踪记录。 因此，下文的一致性结果是将最终的检测器实现与最终的人工复核标注集进行比较所得的。

paragraphs.en: The 14 D-verify disagreements in the reviewed traces fall into four recurring patterns:

paragraphs.en: Repeated calculator calls caused by a stuck loop. The detector interprets the repeated calls as verification, while human review indicates that the model is repeating the computation without making progress.

paragraphs.en: Verbal recognition of an incorrect tool result without an explicit recomputation. In these cases, the trace contains evidence that the model noticed a problem, but not the re-execution pattern expected by D-verify.

paragraphs.en: Together, C1 , C2 , and C3 connect the measurement state, controlled audit, and inspection workflow in Table 2 , supporting one practical conclusion: detector outputs should not be taken at face value. Labels such as “verified,” “correct,” or “fault did not propagate” are produced by measurement procedures that can miss important parts of what happened in the trace. This is visible in several recurring cases. A model may recover without following the detector’s expected pattern, repeated tool calls may be counted as verification even when the model is stuck in a loop, and some propagation questions remain inconclusive because the trace does not contain enough evidence. These differences can disappear once traces are reduced to aggregate scores.
paragraphs.zh: C1、C2 和 C3 共同连接了表 2 中的度量状态、受控审计与检查工作流，支持一个实际结论：检测器的输出不应被当作表面价值直接采信。 诸如「已验证」「正确」或「故障未传播」之类的标签，是由度量程序产生的，而这些程序可能遗漏追踪中发生的重要部分。 这在若干反复出现的案例中清晰可见。 模型可能在没有遵循检测器预期模式的情况下自行恢复，重复的工具调用即使模型陷入循环也可能被计为验证，并且某些传播问题因追踪中证据不足而仍无定论。 一旦追踪被约减为聚合分数，这些差异就可能消失。

paragraphs.en: Silent tool-output override is an especially important example. In our arithmetic setting, a model can receive an incorrect calculator value and later continue with a different, correct value without explicitly re-checking the tool. This can aid recovery from the injected fault. In a setting where the external tool represents a sensor, laboratory result, or financial record, however, silently replacing its output could alter the rest of the workflow without making the change clear. Our experiment does not test such applications directly, but it shows why the original tool output, the value later used by the model, and the detector label should remain visible.
paragraphs.zh: 无声覆盖工具输出是一个特别重要的例子。 在我们的算术场景中，模型可能收到一个错误的计算器数值，之后在不显式重新检查工具的情况下，继续使用另一个正确的数值。 这有助于从注入的故障中恢复。 然而，在外部工具代表传感器、实验室结果或财务记录的场景中，无声替换其输出可能会改变工作流程的其余部分，而不使这一变更显得清晰。 我们的实验并未直接测试此类应用，但它说明了为什么原始工具输出、模型随后使用的数值以及检测器标签都应保持可见。

paragraphs.en: This study has the following limitations that also motivate the next steps for this work. First, the benchmark uses arithmetic word problems. Arithmetic is useful because tool outputs and final answers can be checked against clear external ground truth, but the same detector rules may not transfer directly to domains with free-form, categorical, or subjective outputs. Future work will therefore extend the audit to other datasets and task types, including settings with structured and free-form tool outputs.
paragraphs.zh: 本研究存在以下局限性，这些局限性同时也为后续工作指明了方向。 首先，该基准使用的是算术应用题。 算术问题的价值在于工具输出和最终答案都可以对照明确的外部标准答案进行检验，但同样的检测规则未必能直接迁移到输出为自由文本、类别型或主观性的领域。 因此，未来的工作将把审计扩展到其他数据集和任务类型，包括具有结构化和自由文本工具输出的场景。

sents.zh: 本研究存在以下局限性，这些局限性同时也为后续工作指明了方向。

sents.en: First, the benchmark uses arithmetic word problems.

paragraphs.en: Second, each evaluated model is represented by 30 benchmark traces. This is sufficient to expose recurring measurement failures, but it is a small sample for estimating precise model-level rates. Fault exposure also depends on how often each model calls the calculator, so models that make more tool calls can encounter more injected faults even under the same per-call fault probability. Larger experiments across more questions, models, and traces would provide more stable estimates. Standard 30-trace runs took about 10 minutes, while the full ablation took close to two hours; these are approximate and endpoint-dependent runtimes. Scaling will require parallel or batched execution and more efficient aggregation and visualization.
paragraphs.zh: 其次，每个被评估的模型由 30 条基准测试轨迹表示。 这足以暴露反复出现的测量失败，但用于估计精确的模型级比率时，这只是一个小样本。 故障暴露还取决于每个模型调用计算器的频率，因此在相同的单次调用故障概率下，进行更多工具调用的模型可能遇到更多注入的故障。 跨更多问题、模型和轨迹的更大规模实验将提供更稳定的估计。 标准的 30 条轨迹运行大约耗时 10 分钟，而完整消融实验耗时接近两小时；这些是近似值，且运行时间取决于端点。 扩展规模将需要并行或批量执行，以及更高效的聚合与可视化。

paragraphs.en: Third, the human-label audit uses one primary reviewer. Manual review also revealed coverage gaps in the initial detector logic. We revised the affected rules, reran the automated labels, and re-checked earlier traces; the reported agreement therefore reflects the final detector implementation against the final human-reviewed labels.

paragraphs.en: Finally, the constraint ablation covers two models and two resource controls. It shows that step and token limits can change what is observed, but it does not establish a universal rule for choosing an execution budget. paragraphs.en: Agent evaluation is itself a measurement process. In our controlled audit, detector outputs could be correct under their implemented rules yet still be incomplete or misleading descriptions of the underlying trace. C1 makes that measurement state explicit, C2 shows where the gaps appear in practice, and C3 makes the supporting evidence inspectable. The goal is not to replace automated evaluation, but to make clear when its outputs can be trusted and when the trace deserves closer review.
